title: Bostrom: orthogonality and the control problem
summary: Intelligence and goals are orthogonal. Instrumental convergence pushes almost any goal toward self-preservation and resource acquisition, which defeats boxing, stunting and tripwires. Only approaches that act on the goal structure itself (value learning and corrigibility) coordinate capability with human values.
source: Ch08 8.1 Bostrom — orthogonality thesis, instrumental convergence, control problem

nodes.label: Corrigibility
nodes.description: Accepts correction; humans can modify its goals

nodes.label: Value Learning
nodes.description: Learns human values instead of fixed goals; stays uncertain

nodes.label: True Human Values
nodes.description: What humans would endorse on reflection (CEV)

edges.description: More capability makes instrumental goals easier to pursue
Almost any goal structure converges on the same instrumental goals
Misaligned convergent behaviour leads toward catastrophe
Value learning shapes what the system wants
Corrigibility lets humans modify the goals
Real human values are the target of alignment
Value learning can only approximate them

identifiability_note: True human values (n7) are latent; without access to them we cannot distinguish a truly aligned goal structure from one that merely looks aligned before deployment.
